title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page closes §1 of the notes (Grothendieck's own page numbering 19–20). The next page opens '2. La question de pleine fidélité', so §1 is the FAITHFULNESS half of the anabelian Hom-conjecture for hyperbolic curves. The problem: if two maps of hyperbolic curves induce the same map on (abelianized, profinite) fundamental groups, are they equal? The case treated here is that of open immersions.

Setup from the previous page.
- Y is a hyperbolic curve with smooth completion Ŷ, and U ⊂ Y is open.
- i: U → Y is the inclusion and j: U → Y is another open immersion.
- First step: H_1(i) = H_1(j). This is checked through the generalized Jacobian α: Y → J'_Y, which induces an isomorphism on H_1. Since αj = τ_n ∘ αi with τ_n a translation, and translations act trivially on H_1, the claim follows.
- Put I = Ŷ∖Y and J = Ŷ∖U, so I ⊂ J. Let f ∈ Aut(Ŷ) be the extension of j. Then f(J) ⊃ I.
- Inside H_1(U), the inertia (parabolic) lines L_x for x ∈ J span a copy of Ẑ^J/Ẑ (sum of inertia classes = 0).
- ker H_1(i) is spanned by the L_x with x ∈ J∖I. ker H_1(j) is spanned by the L_x with x ∈ J∖f(I).
- Two such submodules attached to subsets A, A' coincide only if A = A', except when both have cardinality ≥ p−1 (p = card J).

This page.
1. 'Quitte à rapetisser U' Grothendieck assumes card(J∖I) = card(Y∖U) > 1. Then equality of the two kernels forces J∖I = J∖f(I), i.e. f^{-1}(I) = I. So f stabilizes I and restricts to an automorphism of Y.
2. Re-run the argument with Y replaced by Y' = Ŷ∖I', where I' = I∖{i}, i.e. one cusp is filled in. This is allowed as long as Y' is still hyperbolic; the parenthesis is about exactly that condition and the exceptional low-genus cases. It gives that f stabilizes every I∖{i}, hence fixes each cusp. So f is the identity on I.
3. Genus 0: ν = card I ≥ 3 fixed points of a Möbius transformation force f = id.
4. Genus 1: f has a fixed point and acts trivially on H_1, hence f is a translation fixing a point, hence the identity. This is the 'u = 1 / image of u in J°_Ŷ' remark.
5. Genus ≥ 2: 'on termine comme précédemment', presumably the classical fact that an automorphism acting trivially on H_1 (with level ≥ 3) is the identity.

Conclusion: j = i ('Ouf!'). The upshot is that an open immersion between hyperbolic curves is determined by its action on profinite H_1, a faithfulness statement.
errors: The ambiguity in recovering a subset A ⊂ J from the submodule spanned by the L_x, x ∈ A, in Ẑ^J/Ẑ occurs when card A ≥ p−1. Here A = J∖I, so the condition needed is card I ≥ 2 (or a separate treatment of card I ≤ 1). Grothendieck instead writes card(J∖I) > 1 and says this is obtained by shrinking U, which seems not to address the issue directly. This is either a slip or a gap hidden by an unstated reduction; it is easily repairable (e.g. remove extra points to create cusps, or handle the compact/one-cusp cases separately).

The step 'replace Y by Y' = Y ∪ {i}' requires Y' to remain hyperbolic. This fails e.g. for genus 0 with 3 cusps, or genus 1 with 1 cusp. The text acknowledges an exclusion only vaguely; those cases are then handled ad hoc in the genus 0 / genus 1 conclusions.
Several sentences are left grammatically unfinished (e.g. 'f induit un fait un automorphisme'); this is draft-level, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Faithfulness: an open immersion (more generally a dominant morphism) of hyperbolic curves is determined by its action on the profinite (abelianized) fundamental group.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness part of the anabelian Hom-conjecture / injectivity of Hom(U,Y) → Hom^out(π_1U, π_1Y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjectural framework, letter to Faltings 1983); proofs folklore; Mochizuki, Tamagawa, Nakamura for the full Hom statements
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (1981, partial transcription by Malgoire)

ideas.what: Kernel of H_1(U) → H_1(Y) is spanned by the inertia lines at the removed points; the cusp set can be read off from these kernels.
ideas.modern_name: Weight/inertia filtration on H_1 of an affine curve; group-theoretic reconstruction of cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Deligne weights); cusp reconstruction: Nakamura, Tamagawa

ideas.what: Filling in one cusp at a time to show the automorphism fixes each cusp, then rigidity: genus 0 with ≥3 fixed points; genus 1 translation with a fixed point; genus ≥2 trivial action on H_1.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of automorphisms of hyperbolic curves acting trivially on H_1 (Serre–Hurwitz type lemma)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary proof of a faithfulness statement (open immersions of hyperbolic curves are determined by H_1). The statement and techniques are classical, and faithfulness is well known to be the 'easy' half of the anabelian Hom-conjecture. The page is of historical interest only, showing Grothendieck working out the details himself.
transcription_corrections: 'Y' = Y ∪ i' should be 'Y' = Y ∪ {i} = Ŷ∖I''.
'f induit un fait un automorphisme de Y' reads 'f induit un automorphisme de Y'.
'Γ°_Ŷ' is more likely 'J°_Ŷ' (the Jacobian / Pic^0 of Ŷ).
'f = que f induit' should read 'on voit que f induit'.
The parenthesis about 'géodésiques généralisées' is uncertain; it is likely about the condition that Y' still be hyperbolic/anabelian, excluding some genus-1 configurations.
